studies.title: Large-area tetrahedron: face activation and recurrence
studies.description: Exact FL free-hopping control on five/six channels, with four initial tetrahedral spinors and vacuum extras. Twenty controls span K=2..10000 and two phase choices. A fifth channel can take 29.06% of area, while individual areas and local energies recur.
studies.limits: Unit complete-graph hopping, U=0, pure FL manifold. Direct sparse occupation evolution verifies K=1,2. No irreversible equipartition or interacting thermalization established. The two extra symmetric six-channel rows have the same normal, leaving only five distinct classical directions. Phase controls have different conserved initial energies.
studies.status: 360 direct-state, occupation, energy, geometry and recurrence checks passed

studies.title: Entanglement of separately closed thermal polyhedra
studies.description: 86 temperatures over T*=0.05..5. Exact Schmidt eigenvalues and multiplicities yield entropy, area-sector decomposition, purity, Renyi-2 entropy and coherent joint singlet creation. Within-area entanglement exceeds area-distribution entropy at T*=1,2,5.
studies.limits: Normalized double-singlet projection of the area-one F12 reference; initially only two active faces. Ordinary left/right tensor factorization. Adaptive area cutoffs 12..140; entropy truncation estimate below 6.4e-12 nats. Temperature slopes are prepared-state responses; fixed single-copy Gibbs and AdS interpretations are not assumed. General four-face FL inputs remain open.
studies.status: 802 oscillator, spectrum, geometry and convergence comparisons passed

studies.title: Heating separately closed area and positive RS volume

studies.title: Singlet exchange between closed FL polyhedra
studies.description: Fixed combined area K=4, dimension 1210; four Hamiltonians and three FL inputs. Twelve trajectories follow area current, entropy, coherence and positive RS volume; twenty canonical controls retain full joint Gibbs entropy.
studies.limits: Finite isolated pair; prepared-state entanglement differs from mixed-state Gibbs entropy. No reservoir relaxation or equivalence to the T9 squeezed family established. Project volume and model energy units.
studies.status: 46 recorded regression tests and 1792 independent comparisons passed

studies.title: Four versus five sites: thermal-volume persistence
studies.description: Matched mean occupation 2K/L=2: (L,K)=(4,4) and (5,5), singlet dimensions 105 and 1,176. Complete and ring graphs at t=1,U=20, plus free and no-hopping controls. Intermediate-temperature nonmonotonicity persists; the pronounced four-site complete-graph low-temperature collapse does not.
studies.limits: The plot reports volume per selected triple; CSV files also retain total volume. Triple counts: 4 for both four-site graphs, 10 for five-site complete, 5 for five-site ring. Unit hopping per bond, g=0. Coordination changes and the odd ring make this a persistence test, not clean finite-size scaling. Six sites were not calculated.

studies.title: Prepared tetrahedral FL states and the volume crossover
studies.description: Five explicitly constructed K=4 FL references: equal input face areas, phi=90,60,30,10,0 degrees. Saved face-spin distributions, pair correlations, angular fluctuations, volume distributions and overlaps; comparisons with the first three energy groups of complete/ring Hamiltonians at t=1,U=20. The complete ground is kernel-dominated despite nearly unit four-face weight.
studies.limits: FL references are prepared states; energy groups and Gibbs mixtures are separate comparisons. This record contains static readouts; the separate T11 candidate-Hamiltonian record includes geometric-coupling scans and time evolution. Angular normalization is assignment-specific and conditioning retains coherence and selection probabilities. Geometric volume uses the established sqrt(2)/12 four-valent conversion. The Hamiltonian in this record uses g=0. No new independent Rust run.

studies.title: Candidate geometric Hamiltonians and prepared-FL dynamics
studies.description: Exact K=4, total-spin-zero study (dimension 105). The baseline is complete-graph face-to-face area exchange plus on-site repulsion, with equal hopping strength on each bond. We added the positive RS-volume term and the signed triple-grasp term as separate candidate Hamiltonians, then evolved five explicitly prepared FL references under the baseline and both signed couplings. The 62 parameter settings cover U/t=0,1,5,20 and normalized coupling alpha=-2,-1,-0.5,0,0.5,1,2; the ring is included only as a sparse-hopping control. The study contains 6,510 saved energy levels and 50 prepared-state trajectories.
studies.limits: The complete graph represents tetrahedral face adjacency; the ring is a hopping control, not a proposed tetrahedron. The positive-volume and signed-grasp additions are tested candidate models, not derived physical interactions. Results use one copy, fixed K=4, project-normalized volume, and t=1; no physical coupling calibration or phase-transition claim is implied. The long-time dynamics are exact energy-basis samples with adaptive logarithmic coverage, not a uniformly resolved trace of every fast oscillation. Large thermal and dynamics CSVs are gzip-compressed for download; their source and package checksums are both listed.
studies.status: 62 Hamiltonian parameter settings and 50 FL trajectories calculated; 1,510 independent checks passed (maximum residual 1.07e-12)

studies.title: Four-site Hamiltonian spectra and RS-volume observables
studies.description: Exact diagonalization of the hopping-plus-on-site-repulsion operator H_G=-t Σ_(i,j)∈E_G(E_ij+E_ji)+(U/2)Σ_i n_i(n_i−1), where E_ij=a_i†a_j+b_i†b_j and n_i=a_i†a_i+b_i†b_i. Four sites, fixed boson number 2K and total spin zero; K=2,3,4 gives dimensions 20,50,105, with empty sites allowed. Compare the complete graph (6 hopping bonds) and periodic ring (4), with equal t per bond. The 30 cases use (t,U)=(0,1) or t=1 and U/t=0,1,5,20.
studies.limits: The positive Rovelli–Smolin (RS) volume V=(γℏ)^(3/2)Σ_(connected triples)√|q_ijk|, q_ijk=i[J_i·J_j,J_j·J_k], is a separate observable evaluated on energy eigenstates and Gibbs states; it is not a term in H_G, and no g_V V coupling was calculated. The optional spin-exchange setting is g=0. Both graphs select the same four connected triples, so V is the same operator and only the hopping graph changes. Project-normalized volume; physical calibration is open. The temperature response is a finite-sector crossover, not a phase transition. Ground-state entropy uses the Gibbs mixture when degenerate.
